Description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa, working on the final pages of his new translation, takes up the recurring question of what becomes of earlier generations who lacked the complete message, recalling Pharaoh's question to Moses. He answers with a population estimate: about 6 billion people have lived from Adam until 1989, against some 75 billion still to come before the end of the world in 2280, so that the vast majority of humanity will receive the message intact. He revisits the classification of creatures into angels who never doubted God's absolute authority, jinns who accepted Satan's claim, and humans who remained undecided, and argues from Sura 19:71-72, Sura 21:101 and Sura 7:32 that this world is itself a mild or halfway Hell, defined as the absence of God's physical presence and distinguished from the eternal Hell by the fact that God still provides for believer and disbeliever alike, as in Sura 2:126. The second sermon previews a finding credited to Abdullah that stringing together the chapter and verse numbers of the Quran, stopping Sura 9 at verse 127, yields a number miles long that is a multiple of 19, and that the same holds for the units of the five prayers, then reads Malachi 3 on the Messenger of the Covenant and disputes the Christian identification of that figure with John the Baptist.
